title: The 10 Best Cordless Framing Nailers
subtitle: Battery-powered framing nailers for decks, sheds and remodels, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: Cordless framing nailers drive 2 to 3-1/2 inch nails without a compressor, hose or gas cartridge. We ranked 10 best-sellers from DEWALT, Makita, Metabo HPT, CRAFTSMAN and RYOBI on rating, review volume and features (a battery in the box, a light tool body and a warranty of three years or more). The first decision is the nail angle: 21° nailers take plastic-strip nails, 30° nailers take paper-tape nails.

changelog.note: Full audit. Replaced the Milwaukee 2745-20 and the DEWALT DCN930P1 kit, which no longer have a featured seller on Amazon, with the RYOBI PBL350B ($300) and the Makita XNB03Z ($398). The previous tool to avoid, a third-party Milwaukee 2744-20 listing, is gone; the Freeman PE20V2183 takes its place. The three Metabo HPT NR1890 nailers dropped from $449-$459 to $359.
Prices, ratings and review counts re-checked on 9 of 11 listings. Biggest price moves: the DEWALT DCN930P1 rose from $449.99 to $528; the Metabo HPT NR1890DRST rose from $400 to $449.
Page published with 10 ranked picks and 1 tool to avoid.

avoid.name: Freeman 20V Cordless 21° Framing Nailer Kit, 750 Shots per Charge (PE20V2183)
avoid.flag: 3.1 stars, 1-year warranty, battery fits only Freeman tools
avoid.verdict: A $311 kit that costs about what a bare CRAFTSMAN or RYOBI framer does, but buyers rate it 3.1 stars and Freeman backs it for one year. Spend the same on a name-brand bare tool, or on the CRAFTSMAN CMCN621PLB if you need a battery platform with more tools.
reasons: Buyers rate it 3.1 out of 5, the lowest of any cordless framer we checked.
The warranty is Freeman's 1-year limited warranty; most nailers on this page carry 3 years or more.
The 20V 4.0Ah battery fits Freeman's own small cordless line, so it won't run the drills and saws most people already own.
Amazon files it under Power Finish Nailers rather than framing nailers, a sign the listing hasn't been kept up.

buyers_guide.a: It comes down to the nails you can buy locally and your building code. 21° nailers take plastic-strip full round head nails. 30° (and 30-34°) nailers take paper-tape nails, usually clipped head, and the magazine is shorter so it fits between studs more easily. Check that full round head nails aren't required where you build before going 30° with clipped heads.

buyers_guide.q: Are cordless framing nailers as good as pneumatic?
buyers_guide.a: For decks, sheds, remodels and punch-out work, yes: no compressor, no hose, and the better ones fire 2 to 3 nails per second. Full-time production framers still tend to use pneumatic because the tools are lighter and never need charging.
A cordless framer carries its own motor and drive system, so most weigh 8 to 11 lb before you add the battery. The Metabo HPT kits are the lightest here at 8.2 to 8.4 lb.

buyers_guide.q: Should I buy the bare tool or a kit?
buyers_guide.a: If you already own batteries on the same platform, buy the bare tool and use your largest battery. If not, a kit is usually the cheaper way in than buying a bare tool, battery and charger separately.
The listings here claim about 500 to 1,100 per charge, depending on the battery. Use a 4.0Ah or larger battery for framing; small compact packs run out fast and can struggle to sink 3-1/2 inch nails.
